items.title: Roosevelt Charles Interview
items.q: The leader of number one would go to Holland, John Henry.

ctx.x: The story that I'm about to tell was back in 1937 when times was hard and weeks was hard. The balls were very hard. The inmates, they were very cruel sometimes themselves. You'd get out on the job sometime early in the morning. We would be drowsing, feeling bad. The leader of number one would go to Holland, John Henry. That means pick your two up high and let them fall together. Boys then the light would hit the game. They would start rolling on. Every now and then you call the water-boy and the water-boy-

He said to some sticking out the little holes up top trying to get out through them, but it was no way out that they could get out. Mother's sons and daughters had slipped off from home. Right now today, there's mothers don't know where daughters at. Fathers don't know why sons at. Sons don't know why mother and brothers don't know why sister.
